name: Nurturing Skills for Families About Me Page 1
notes: Nurturing Skills Competency Scale page 1. Most numbered response fields are short letter-entry lines where the respondent writes the selected answer letter from the visible choices. Question notes list the visible choices. gender_other belongs to Question 6 option e Other. nationality belongs to the visible Nationality line under Question 7 Race/Nationality.

inputDefinitions.placeholderText: Enter name of person administering inventory

inputDefinitions.label: Question 6 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 6: Gender. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Male; b Female; c Transgender Man; d Transgender Woman; e Other. If e Other is selected, use input gender_other for the written other gender value.

inputDefinitions.label: Gender other
inputDefinitions.notes: Free-text Other value for Question 6 Gender option e Other.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 7 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 7: Race/Nationality. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a White; b Black; c Asian; d Hispanic; e Native American; f Pacific Islander; g Bi-racial; h Multi-racial; i Other. The separate nationality input captures the visible Nationality line below this question.

inputDefinitions.label: Nationality
inputDefinitions.notes: Free-text Nationality line associated with Question 7 Race/Nationality; this is not the Question 7 letter answer field.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 8 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 8: Marital Status. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Single; b Married; c Unmarried Partners; d Separated/Divorced; e Widow/Widower.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 9 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 9: Number of children you have. Enter the respondent's number of children; this field is paired with the visible Number of children line.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 10 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 10: Highest grade you completed. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Grade School; b Middle School (grades 7 & 8); c Some High School (grades 9-11); d High School Graduate; e Working on or Completed GED; f Two Year Tech School; g Some College; h College Graduate; i Post Graduate or above.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 11 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 11: Current Employment-School status. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Employed full-time; b Going to school full-time; c Employed part-time; d Going to school part-time; e Both going to school and working; f I am a stay-at-home Mom or Dad; g Currently unemployed and not going to school; h Retired; i Other. There is no separate other-text overlay on this page for option i.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 12 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 12: Annual Household Income. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Under $15,000; b $15,001 to $25,000; c $25,001 to $30,000; d $30,001 to $40,000; e $40,001 to $60,000; f Over $60,000; g I don't know.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 13 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 13: Are or were you and/or your partner in the military? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes, only me; b Yes, only my partner; c Yes, both of us; d No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 14 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 14: As a child, did you experience any type of physical, emotional or sexual abuse by someone outside of your family? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes; b No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 15 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 15: As a child, did you experience any type of physical, emotional or sexual abuse by someone inside of your family? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes; b No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 16 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 16: Ever feel that no one in your family loved you or thought you were special? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes; b No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 17 answer

inputDefinitions.label: Question 18 answer

inputDefinitions.label: Question 21 answer

inputDefinitions.notes: Question 22: Ever feel your father or father figure was physically, verbally or sexually abused by his partner? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes, and I witnessed the abuse; b Yes, but I didn't witness the abuse; c No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 23 answer

inputDefinitions.label: Question 24 answer

inputDefinitions.label: Question 25 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 25: Is your parent partner a problem drinker or alcoholic; abuses prescription drugs or uses street drugs? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes; b No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 26 answer

inputDefinitions.label: Question 28 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 28: Has your parent partner physically, verbally or sexually abused you? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes; b No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 29 answer

inputDefinitions.label: Question 30 answer

inputDefinitions.label: Question 31 answer

name: Nurturing Skills for Families Children, Family, and Knowledge Page 3
notes: Nurturing Skills Competency Scale page 3. All numbered inputs on this page are short letter-entry lines where the respondent writes the selected answer letter from the visible choices for Questions 32-48. There are no separate Other text fields on this page.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 32 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 32: Have any of your children ever experienced any type of physical, verbal or sexual abuse by a person outside your family? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes; b No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 33 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 33: Have any of your children ever experienced any type of physical, verbal or sexual abuse by a person inside your family? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes; b No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 34 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 34: Do any of your children currently have or had in the past problems with alcohol, prescription drugs or street drugs? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes; b No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 35 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 35: Do any of your children have special learning needs that require a specialist or special education? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes; b No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 36 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 36: Do any of your children have a history of mental health problems? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes; b No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 37 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 37: Has anyone in your family ever been referred for psychological counseling? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes; b No.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 38 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 38: Overall, I would rate my parenting skills. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Very Good; b Good; c Bad; d Very Bad.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 39 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 39: Overall, the degree of happiness I feel being a parent is. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a High; b OK; c Low; d Very Low.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 40 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 40: Knowing what you know now about being a parent, would you still be a parent if you could do it all over again? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Yes; b Probably; c Probably Not; d Absolutely Not.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 41 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 41: Nurturing Parenting is. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Being a parent 24 hours a day, 365 days a year; b Nurturing your children and yourself; c Making sure the needs of children always come first; d Teaching children to care for others.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 42 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 42: Giving children choices early in life teaches them to make good decisions later in life. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Giving children choices will never get them to do what you want them to do; b Kids can't handle choices - they feel more secure being told what to do; c Choices can help children learn that there are consequences to the decisions they make; d Kids who have choices generally get into power struggles with their parents.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 43 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 43: Having appropriate expectations for children helps them. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Learn to feel good about themselves; b Develop trust and security; c Learn to succeed in school; d All the above statements are true.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 44 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 44: Discipline means. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a To guide children by using the rod of correction; b To guide children in learning proper morals; c To teach children to be obedient; d To guide children to learn to respect elders.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 45 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 45: The rights and wrongs that children learn are called. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Family Morals; b Family Values; c Family Traditions; d Family Customs.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 46 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 46: Empathy means. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a To be aware of the feelings your children express; b To feel what it's like being a child; c To help children get their needs met; d Empathy can be all of these at different times.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 47 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 47: Fear teaches children to respect parent's authority. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Fear teaches children to disrespect their parents; b It's ok to use fear as long as parents don't overdo it; c Fear teaches children to respect the law; d Fear teaches children to learn to be obedient.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 48 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 48: Children who have a strong sense of personal power. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Get into power struggles with parents about everything; b Are less influenced by peer pressure; c Is one of the characteristics of a bully; d Have difficulty sharing things with others.

name: Nurturing Skills for Families Knowledge and Utilization Page 4
notes: Nurturing Skills Competency Scale page 4. Questions 49-60 are short letter-entry lines where the respondent writes the selected answer letter from visible choices a-d. Questions 61-73 are radio rating rows for Part F utilization, where 0 means Don't practice the skill at all, 1 means Sometimes, 2 means Often, and 3 means Regularly. There are no separate Other text fields on this page.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 49 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 49: Pick the right way to Praise a child for Being. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a You are such a good child for helping me; b You make me feel so happy when you get good grades; c You are a wonderful child; d You are such a nice girl when you cooperate.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 50 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 50: Which of the following are good rewards to use as discipline? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Praise and some hugs; b Privilege like staying up a little later; c Gifts like toys, CDs, DVDs; d At times, all these are good rewards to use.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 51 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 51: Family rules are important because. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Children need to learn to be obedient; b Children need to learn how to cooperate; c Children need to respect authority; d Children need to listen to their parents.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 52 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 52: Why do parents spank their children? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a The Bible says spare the rod, spoil the child; b Because parents were spanked as children; c Because they love their children; d Parents spank children for all these reasons.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 53 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 53: Which of the following is a healthy way to manage and reduce stress? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Use a punching bag to release your energy; b Get away and leave your kids for a while; c Exercise daily and practice deep breathing; d It depends on what works for the parents - everybody is different.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 54 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 54: Pick the right way to Praise a child for Doing. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Good job cleaning your room - mommy really loves you; b You really sing well; c You did pretty well - next time try harder; d Do well and make your family proud of you.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 55 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 55: Teaching children to hit a pillow or punching bag is a good way for them to release their anger. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Hitting is a good way to release anger energy; b Hitting teaches kids to hit when they're angry; c Hitting is OK as long as you don't get carried away; d Hitting something is a very quick way to calm down.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 56 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 56: Our self-worth is. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Developed from the ways others think about us; b The thoughts and feelings we have about ourselves; c Learned in childhood and is difficult to change; d Depends upon the opinions of others.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 57 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 57: Teaching children the correct names for their sexual body parts. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Is the first step in building positive sexual self-worth; b Helps children feel good about their bodies; c Helps children learn to say No to unwanted touch; d All of the above.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 58 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 58: The best way to help children understand their feelings is to. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Listen quietly and attentively; b Respect the child's feelings; c Encourage the child to talk; d All of the above.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 59 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 59: Anger is. Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Past hurt feelings that are finally being expressed; b Anger is a feeling that causes people to become violent; c Getting angry is a good way to release stress; d Anger lets others know you are mad at them.

inputDefinitions.label: Question 60 answer
inputDefinitions.notes: Question 60: Which of the following is a good way to build self-worth in children? Enter the selected letter. Choices: a Listen and honor their opinions; b Provide children with choices and consequences for their behavior; c Don't blame them for the way parents feel; d All of these are good ways to build self-worth.
